title: A Neighbourhood Power Cut
instructions: Listen carefully. Choose the option that best matches what is said or implied.

audio.description: Residents discuss a short power cut and how to check on others.

transcript.text: The lights went out after six; repairs may take two hours. My phone is nearly flat, so I am saving its battery.
The radio says the fault is in the street cabinet. A team is there, but there is no exact estimate.
I cannot use the hob. Does the small shop have a generator?
It was open, but its card machine was down, so it took cash. I can check on the older couple next door.
Would you? They use an electric stair lift, so I hope they are all right. I will leave a torch outside.
Good idea. If power is still off at eight, we can share food from my freezer before it thaws.

questions.prompt: What does the radio report about the cause?
options: A fault in the street cabinet
A planned repair to the shop
A problem with mobile phone signals
questions.explanation: The resident says the radio identifies the street cabinet as the location of the problem.

questions.prompt: Why is the shop accepting cash only?
options: It has run out of change.
Its card machine is not working.
The power has already returned there.
questions.explanation: The resident saw that the shop was open but its card machine was down.

questions.prompt: Why does Resident A ask the neighbour to check on the older couple?
options: They have no food in the house.
They may depend on an electric stair lift.
They are responsible for the repair team.
They cannot use a battery radio.
questions.explanation: Resident A specifically mentions that the couple use an electric stair lift and hopes they are all right.

questions.prompt: What are the residents planning to do if the outage continues?
options: Contact the repair team every few minutes.
Share food from the freezer before it thaws.
questions.explanation: They agree that if power is still off by eight, they can share the freezer food before it begins to thaw.
